doc: Preregistration for M5 iterations (docs/BUILD_PLAN.md §0.1). One key per iteration under iterations, each in its own source spec/M5/predictions/<key>.json (holon.aggregate writes this aggregate from them). A key is written once, in its prereg commit, before any of its outcome_paths change; holon audit prereg checks the order and that the key is never edited afterwards. predictions count toward prediction accuracy; regressions are outcomes already recorded in the repo that must not change.

I54.title: I54: L6, L9 and L10 defined and preregistered (Q11): bounded games scored against constructed and documented truth, environment coverage by validated time-indexed modules, intent-law coverage over a mechanical clause census

contracts/contracts/l1/rollup/Rollup.sol contributes more census clauses than any other file in that scope.
At least a quarter of that census's clauses come from .go files.

Under the frozen classification, 222 of the M2 and M3 result records at the base are environment-dependent (A-env havoc in 222, the env: axiom in 4), none is covered, and no id is unclassified; they are base.l9_dependent.

common.doc: Shared rules of L6, L9 and L10. A metric reads records and truth files and nothing else; it runs no checker and trusts no field it can recompute.
common.proportion: every proportion is reported as {numerator, denominator, value, wilson95}; value is null when the denominator is 0 (never 0.0 or 1.0); wilson95 is the Wilson score interval at z = 1.96, rounded to 4 places, null when the denominator is 0
common.labels: a measure is 'measured' when its denominator is at least min_n, 'insufficient_n' when it is 1..min_n-1, 'not_measured' when it is 0 or an input is absent (with the reason). A threshold is judged 'meets' or 'misses' only for a measured measure; otherwise its verdict is the measure's label, never 'meets'
common.outcome_vocabulary: statuses are exactly PROVED, REFUTED and UNKNOWN; a verdict counts as decided only when the record carries checker evidence: evidence.marker is 'ALL PROOFS CHECK' and evidence.law_present is true (AGENTS rule 6). A record that fails a validity rule is scored as UNKNOWN and listed with the rule it failed
common.one_record: a finding, control, clause or law with more than one record is scored as UNKNOWN (no choice among runs); a population member with no record is UNKNOWN
common.truth_pinning: a truth file (controls, corpus truth, observation sets) is read with its sha256, which the output reports; the key that measures L6, L9 or L10 pins those sha256 in its prereg, so truth cannot follow the outputs
common.independence: no truth input is produced by the code it scores: controls by holon.m5.controls (fixed at I54, before any game or intent engine exists), corpus truth by spec/M5/lib/truth_protocol.json from the corpus's verbatim text, history by an observation set whose producer reads none of the module's parameters (L9 R3)
common.split_by_source: accuracy against constructed truth (controls) and against documented truth (corpus, history) is reported separately and never pooled into one number
common.determinism: outputs are json.dumps(obj, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + newline; sorted iteration; no timestamps
common.overall: each metric's overall verdict is meets iff every one of its thresholds meets, misses iff some threshold misses, not_judged otherwise; a metric is reported as meeting its preregistered level only by its overall verdict
common.zero_counts: a threshold of the form count == 0 is judged when its population is measured (at least min_n items); sensitivity_unreplayed is judged when at least one status changed
common.special_casing: no module of holon/ other than holon/m5/controls.py may hold a control's id or name token; the engines that I55-I57 build are target-agnostic (BUILD_PLAN §2)

L6.name: can versus will: bounded games over the REFUTED findings (Q11)
L6.population: F(M): the result records results/<M>/L_*.json with status REFUTED and filter_bin not in {model_defect, known_limitation, intended_bounded}, for each measured milestone M (M3 at the I54 base; M5's when it has records); a record moved out of F after the I54 base is listed with its new bin (base_population)
L6.base_population: the law ids of F(M3) at the I54 base, frozen in spec/M5/preregistration.json (base.l6_findings)
L6.record: spec/M5/lib/inputs.schema.json#/$defs/game_record, one per finding, control or corpus item
L6.actors: the game's classes are the target's principal classes (holon.diagram principal_classes), each with its trusted flag; the trusted flags of a target are fixed by a sidecar preregistered before its first game record, and the controls' by their documents
L6.ordinal_payoff: a class's payoff under a strategy is the sign vector of its holdings' change per asset of the extracted value flows (transfers, rewards, deposits, slashing, protocol fees; transaction gas is outside the flows, premise P-gas): nonneg iff no component is negative; negative iff no component is positive and some is negative; incomparable otherwise. No exchange rate between assets is assumed
L6.semantics: a strategy of class X is a schedule of actions that X may call (others take no action, environment moves allowed), within the game's horizon H; it triggers the finding when the finding's state predicate holds after some step; its payoff is taken at the schedule's end
L6.class_verdict: rational: some triggering strategy has payoff nonneg; irrational: every triggering strategy has payoff negative (or none triggers), proved over every schedule (scope unbounded); irrational_bounded: the same proved only for schedules up to H; UNKNOWN otherwise (incomparable payoffs included)
L6.finding_verdict: rational iff some untrusted class is rational; irrational iff every untrusted class is irrational; irrational_bounded iff every untrusted class is irrational or irrational_bounded and some is bounded; UNKNOWN otherwise. Trusted classes are reported, never decide the verdict

validity.V2: the record's classes are exactly the expected classes of its finding (the target's principal classes, or the control's actors), by id
validity.V3: each class's trusted flag equals the expected one
validity.V4: horizon >= witness_length, and witness_length equals the length of the finding's REFUTED witness (a control's witness)
validity.V5: witness_in_space is true: the finding's own witness is a strategy of the game (non-vacuity of the strategy space)
validity.V6: the record's verdict is the finding_verdict of its classes
validity.V7: a rational class has payoff nonneg and strategy_length between 1 and horizon
validity.V8: value_flows_sha256 equals the expected one: for a target, the sha256 of the value-flow facts document fixed in the sidecar of its trusted flags; for a control, the sha256 of the canonical JSON (sort_keys, separators ',' ':') of its actions

measures.decided: over F: records whose validated verdict is rational, irrational or irrational_bounded / |F| (headline, per milestone); also decided_unbounded, which does not count irrational_bounded
measures.verdicts: counts of rational, irrational, irrational_bounded and UNKNOWN over F, and the invalid records with their rules
measures.accuracy: per truth source (controls; corpus): over items with truth rational or irrational or UNKNOWN; an item is correct iff its validated verdict equals its truth, irrational_bounded counting as irrational. decided_accuracy = correct decided / decided; strict_accuracy = correct / items (an UNKNOWN verdict on a decided truth is wrong; on an UNKNOWN truth it is right)
measures.majority_baseline: per truth source: the number of items of the most frequent truth value; strict correct must exceed it
measures.false_rational: per truth source: items with truth irrational whose validated verdict is rational (the negative control of Q11)
measures.false_irrational: per truth source: items with truth rational whose validated verdict is irrational or irrational_bounded (the deep controls test bounded results read as global, L17)
measures.decided_on_unknown: per truth source: items with truth UNKNOWN whose validated verdict is decided

L6.corpus_mapping: a finding is a corpus item iff its record comes from a run on the entry's pre-fix commit (I51) and its law's source spans meet a line the entry's fix changes; each entry with a truth value contributes one item per mapped finding; an entry whose truth is undocumented contributes none; c13 never (spec/M5/lib/truth_protocol.json known_exclusions)

L9.name: environment: time-indexed environment modules (Q11)
L9.environment_premises: E(r) of a result record r: each ledger_assumptions or model_assumptions id, and each premise string with a listed prefix, that the classification marks environment (category, form); plus every premise of r's environment block (spec/M5/lib/inputs.schema.json#/$defs/environment_block). An id the classification does not list and no pattern matches is 'unclassified': it counts as an environment axiom of category unclassified
L9.implicit: a record of a law whose model reads an environment carrier (the diagram's carriers of class env, the blob-hash vector, or a fetcher call) without a premise for it gets, from the generator that writes its environment block, a premise of form axiom for that carrier's category. A record without an environment block has only its classified ids
L9.population: every result record results/<M>/L_*.json of each measured milestone (M2 and M3 at the I54 base, and M5's)
L9.environment_dependent: r is environment-dependent iff E(r) is not empty
L9.covered: an environment-dependent r is covered iff every element of E(r) has form module and names a module that is validated (R1-R5); axiom, havoc and unclassified are assumed, not modelled

module_families.doc: the parametric families a module may belong to; the metric recomputes every prediction from the module's parameters and the observation, so a module record carries no predictions of its own
module_families.window: parameters {W}; an observation {t, q, observed}: predicted = (q - t <= W) (e.g. blob retrievable from the DA layer at query time q for a blob of time t)
module_families.finality_depth: parameters {d}; an observation {t, head, observed}: scored only when head - t >= d, predicted true (the block at t stays canonical); observed is whether it did
module_families.availability: parameters {}; an observation {t, committed, observed}: predicted = committed (a fetcher returns exactly the committed items)

validation.R1: every observation set the module cites is admissible: its reads share no name with the module's parameter names, and its producer is not one of the module's producers (non-circularity: e.g. a fetch that chose its source by the same retention window is not truth for that window)
validation.R2: the observations, ordered by t (then by set and position), are cut into K contiguous slices of equal size (the last takes the remainder); with provenance premise every slice is held out; with fit_slice_0 slice 0 is excluded and the others are held out
validation.R3: every held-out slice has at least slice_min_n scored observations
validation.R4: every held-out slice has accuracy (predicted == observed) at least slice_accuracy
validation.R5: the scored observations hold at least min_n observed true and min_n observed false (a module that is right only because history holds one class is not validated)
validation.R6: the module's parameters equal the values the measuring key pinned in its prereg, before its observations were scored (a parameter chosen from the evaluation data is a fit, whatever its declared provenance)

measures.coverage: covered / (environment-dependent plus the base laws that are no longer environment-dependent), over the population (headline, per milestone and in total): dropping a premise never raises it
measures.base_coverage: the same over the base population (the law ids environment-dependent at the I54 base, frozen in base.l9_dependent); a base law that is no longer environment-dependent is counted as uncovered and listed (dropping a premise never raises coverage)
measures.by_category: environment-dependent and covered counts per category (l1_chain, da, fetcher, unclassified) and per form
measures.modules: per module: admissible sets, per-slice n and accuracy, the worst held-out slice, R1-R5 and validated
measures.sensitivity: over the sensitivity pairs (spec/M5/lib/inputs.schema.json#/$defs/sensitivity_pair): a pair counts iff status_axiom != status_module, status_module is PROVED or REFUTED, its evidence passes common.outcome_vocabulary, and replay is passed. counted, unreplayed (a change without a passed replay), to_unknown (a decided status that became UNKNOWN; reported, never counted) and the list of counted laws
measures.new_coverage: covered / environment-dependent, over the environment-dependent laws outside the base population

validated_categories.of: the categories with at least one validated module

known_inadmissible.results/M2/historical/index.json source: holon/historical/fetch.py chose the beacon or the archive by its own retention constant (RETENTION_SLOTS, RETENTION_MARGIN), so which source served a blob is not truth for a retention window (R1). The index's retrievability of every committed blob (62 192 of 62 192, KZG-checked) is truth for an availability module, but it holds no observed false (R5)

L9.extension: the classification is extended only by a file whose sha256 the measuring key pins in its prereg, which adds ids (each naming the base id it splits, e.g. a split of A-env into its L1 and its call terms) and never changes a base entry; the output lists the extension's ids

L10.name: consistently wrong code: intent-law coverage (whitepaper L10 metric) and intent extraction quality (its residual risk)

census.doc: the denominator: every normative documentation clause in scope, computed mechanically before any intent law exists, so the atomizer cannot set it
census.scope: for each extracted facts document of the measured milestone (spec/M2/facts/*.extracted.json and spec/M3/facts/*.extracted.json at the I54 base for M3), the paths it cites as <path>:<line> with a .sol or .go suffix, read from its target.repo at its target.commit (the checkout config/holon.json extract.sources names, through git, never its working tree); a cited path absent at that commit is listed as unresolved and excluded
census.comments: Solidity: a run of consecutive lines whose first non-blank characters are ///, and each /** ... */ block. Go: a run of consecutive // lines whose next line (after the run) begins, after indentation, with func, type, var or const. The comment markers (///, //, /**, */, a leading *) and indentation are removed from each line
census.segments: within a comment, a NatSpec tag (@ followed by letters, colons and hyphens) at the start of a line starts a new segment, and so does a blank line; a segment's text is its lines joined with one space, whitespace collapsed
census.sentences: a segment is split after each '.', ';', '!' or '?' that is followed by whitespace or ends the segment
census.normative: a sentence is a clause iff, lower-cased, it contains one of the markers as a whole word or phrase (bounded by non-letters): must, must not, shall, should, only, cannot, can not, never, always, revert, reverts, reverted, require, requires, required, ensure, ensures, guarantee, guarantees, at most, at least, exactly, invariant, forbidden, not allowed
census.id: sha256 of '<file>:<first line>:<text>' in UTF-8, first 16 hex digits; lines are the 1-based first and last line of the segment the sentence came from
census.base: results/M5/l10_census_base.json: the census of M3's scope on the target's pinned commit, written in I54's build
census.tag: each clause records its segment's NatSpec tag (the leading @word), or null

L10.atomized: spec/M5/lib/inputs.schema.json#/$defs/atom_clause: the intent lane's clause records (I55), each with its exact span
L10.covers: an intent law covers a census clause iff one of its clauses is an atomized clause in the same file whose line range meets the census clause's

validity.W1: checker evidence (common.outcome_vocabulary) for status PROVED or REFUTED
validity.W2: review.verdict is faithful and review.reviewer differs from review.compiler
validity.W3: every clause it names is an atomized clause

measures.coverage: census clauses covered by a law that passes W1-W3 / census clauses (headline: intent-law coverage)
measures.compiled_coverage: census clauses covered by a law that passes W3 / census clauses
measures.precision: atomized clauses whose span meets some census clause / atomized clauses
measures.recall: census clauses met by some atomized clause / census clauses
measures.review: laws with review.verdict faithful and an independent reviewer / laws
measures.control_recall: intent controls with truth obstruction true that have a law passing W1-W2 with control set to the control's id and status REFUTED / such controls
measures.false_obstruction: intent controls with truth obstruction false that have a law passing W1-W2 with that control id and status REFUTED
measures.corpus_recall: corpus entries with l10 truth yes and an intent obstruction on their pre-fix commit / such entries (min_n applies; reported when I55 runs on the corpus)

controls.doc: constructed truth, written by holon.m5.controls into spec/M5/controls/ in I54's build, equal to tests_m5/_i54.py's documents; truth recomputed by the instrument's interpreter (K1-K3 of tests_m5/test_m5_definitions.py)

game_families.free_trigger: an untrusted actor triggers with no value flow: rational
game_families.recoup: an untrusted actor deposits, triggers and withdraws: payoff nonneg at the end, rational (a payoff read at the trigger says irrational)
game_families.deep: an untrusted actor triggers only after horizon + 1 steps: rational beyond the horizon (irrational_bounded is wrong)
game_families.trusted_only: only a trusted actor can trigger: irrational (negative control)
game_families.costly: an untrusted actor triggers only by paying a deposit it cannot recover: irrational (negative control)
game_families.incomparable: an untrusted actor triggers, gaining one asset and losing another: UNKNOWN

controls.game_semantics: single deviator: one class acts, the others take no action; each action at most once per schedule; holdings start at 0; payoff at the schedule's end

intent_families.bound: a documented upper bound on a returned fee; the code's rate exceeds it (obstruction) or does not
intent_families.access: a documented 'only the owner' restriction; the code checks the owner (no obstruction) or does not (obstruction)
intent_families.monotone: a documented 'never decreases' counter; the code adds (no obstruction) or subtracts (obstruction)

controls.seed: the instance number and family name; names are the first 6 hex digits of sha256('<family>/<n>/<role>')

thresholds.base: 4fd64a52 (the lead after #131), the parent of I54's prereg commit; base populations are read from this commit's tree through git

I54b.title: I54b: the corpus-truth key: I54's frozen truth protocol run on I48's 20 entries by two fresh labellers per entry, every text, packet and rule pinned before any labeller answers

predictions.claim: In the same-family truth, at least 5 entries other than c13 get an L6 truth (rational or irrational), so L6's corpus accuracy can reach min_n.
In the same-family truth, at most 3 entries other than c13 get L6 truth irrational (the corpus negative control of false_rational stays small).
In the same-family truth, between 1 and 3 entries get L10 truth yes.
Labellers a and b give the same raw trigger value (before Q1-Q2) for at least 14 of the 20 entries.
At most 4 of the 120 same-family answers (20 entries x 2 labellers x 3 questions) fail Q2 (a quote that is not an exact substring of the text).

regressions.claim: spec/eval/corpus.json, truth_protocol.json, truth_prompt.md and the frozen invocation's source are byte-identical to the pins (I48's corpus and I54's protocol are unchanged).
truth_protocol.json and truth_prompt.md hash to I54's own instrument pins.
Between the base commit and HEAD only I54b's paths change: no file of M0-M4, no frozen file, nothing in holon/ or tools/.

thresholds.texts: truth_protocol.json inputs.text: entry title + "\n" + description, verbatim from spec/eval/corpus.json; pins.texts holds the sha256 of each entry's UTF-8 text, for all 20 entries (c13 included: it is labelled like every entry; known_exclusions removes it from scoring, not from labelling)

packets.path: spec/M5/truth/packets/<id>.<role>.txt, role a or b, with spec/M5/truth/packets/index.json (truth_labels.schema.json#/$defs/packet_index)
packets.content: spec/M5/lib/truth_prompt.md with its one {{TEXT}} slot replaced, in one pass, by the entry's text; nothing else (no entry id, system, repository, source URL, fix commit, file list, label or justification beyond what the verbatim text itself holds). The packets of roles a and b of one entry are byte-identical; each is pinned on its own
packets.pins: pins.packets: the sha256 of each packet's UTF-8 bytes, computed at the prereg from the pinned prompt and texts

answer.message: the labeller's final message is one JSON object (truth_labels.schema.json#/$defs/answer_object), the whole message or the whole message inside one fenced block (``` or ```json first line, ``` last line): I48's parse_response. Values are strings and quotes strings or null; a value outside its list is not a shape error (Q1 makes it undocumented)
answer.file: spec/M5/truth/answers/<family>/<id>.<role>.json (truth_labels.schema.json#/$defs/answer_file), one per entry and labeller, written only by python -m tests_m5._i54b answer (sessions) or run (the frozen invocation); every attempt is kept with its outcome
answer.commit: no answer file is committed or pushed before every one of its family's 40 answers is recorded: the 40 same-family answer files are added in exactly one commit (and the different-family ones, if any, in one commit), so no labeller can read another's committed answer (T5). A different-family labeller is never given access to the repository
answer.retry: I48's rule (corpus_protocol.json labelling_invocation.retry) with this protocol's answer: an attempt that gave no answer (cli_error, or no_response for a session) is retried, at most 5; an attempt that is not an answer (turns, unparsable, invalid) is followed by exactly one more; the answer is the last attempt's when ok, else null (every question undocumented). A retry is a new fresh process or session, never a follow-up message

agreement.Q1: a value outside its question's list, or a non-null quote with undocumented, makes that answer undocumented
agreement.Q2: a quote that is not a string, or whose whitespace-collapsed form (Python re \s+ to one space, nothing stripped) is not a substring of the text's collapsed form, makes that answer undocumented (a non-undocumented value with a null quote fails Q2)
agreement.Q3: per question, the final value is a's when a and b both answered, both pass Q1-Q2 and give the same value; otherwise undocumented. There is no adjudicator; every disagreement and rule failure is listed in the run sidecar and never resolved
agreement.derived: l6 and l10 exactly as truth_protocol.json derived
agreement.empty_quote: Q2 is applied literally: a quote that is empty or whitespace only is a substring of every text and passes; the run sidecar lists every such quote (empty_quotes) so the measuring key and the human see them; they are never dropped or rewritten by the builder
agreement.builder: the builder runs no labeller, writes no answer and resolves nothing

outputs.same: spec/M5/truth/corpus.json (the protocol's output path and format, truth_labels.schema.json#/$defs/truth_file) and spec/M5/truth/corpus.run.json (invocations, protocol_exact_invocation, model_check, disagreements, rule_failures, tally, per-answer outcomes and file sha256)
outputs.different: spec/M5/truth/corpus_different.json and corpus_different.run.json, the same rules over answers/different/
outputs.comparison: spec/M5/truth/family_comparison.json: per entry and per question the two families' final values, and equal/differ counts; pooled false
outputs.scoring_truth: the key that measures L6 or L10 on the corpus pins the sha256 of the truth file it reads (I54 common.truth_pinning). The same-family file is the protocol's; a different-family file is reported beside it and never pooled with it
outputs.collector: python -m tests_m5._i54b collect --family F [--check]: refuses, writing nothing, unless every frozen input hashes to its pin and every one of the 40 answer files of F passes truth_labels.schema.json, its path, role tag, invocation, packet path and packet_sha256 (the pin and the packet file's bytes), every attempt's recomputed outcome, the retry rule, and answer = the last ok attempt's parsed message. Deterministic

roles.a: model tag A: the family's most capable model available
roles.b: model tag B: a smaller model of the same family, different from A

labellers.independence: truth_protocol.json invocation, I48's labelling_invocation unchanged: one fresh process per prompt (an entry and a role), nothing else run in it. So the labelling takes exactly 40 fresh labellers (20 entries x 2 roles); no labeller sees two packets, another's answer, a label or a HOLON output
labellers.model_names: never recorded in the repository; only the tags A and B
labellers.family_default: same-family (Q9 default, the Q9b precedent): recorded as family same, and disclosed wherever corpus truth is reported as a limitation: the labellers share the builders' model family, so their independence comes from fresh contexts only
labellers.family_different: if the human has an external agent of another family label (Q9a), it reads the same 40 packets, its answers go to answers/different/ (invocation external, tags A and B for its two labellers), its truth is corpus_different.json, and it is compared with the same-family truth (family_comparison.json), never pooled
labellers.launcher: the coordinator launches every labeller; the builder launches none

invocation.cli: protocol-exact: python -m tests_m5._i54b run --role a --model <A> then --role b --model <B>, from a checkout: each packet in its own fresh `claude -p` process with corpus_protocol.json labelling_invocation's argv, system prompt, environment (env_removed dropped), fresh empty working directory under /tmp, stdin and timeout; tool-less; the model each call reports (modelUsage) is checked per tag outside the repository (one_model_per_role, a_differs_from_b). 40 processes, no cloud session
invocation.cloud_session: a deviation from the frozen invocation, admitted only as disclosed: one fresh cloud session per packet (40), with no repository, whose first and only user message is the packet's bytes and whose appended system prompt is labelling_invocation.system_prompt; model per role as the tags say; the final message is recorded verbatim with python -m tests_m5._i54b answer --invocation cloud_session. It departs from the frozen invocation in that the session has tools (web access, and the account's repositories), num_turns is not checked, and the model is declared, not observed; the run sidecar records protocol_exact_invocation false and model_check declared
invocation.external: the different-family path only: an external agent at the human's request (Q9a), one fresh context per packet, recorded with --invocation external
invocation.recommended: cli: the only invocation that is the frozen one, and the only one in which a labeller cannot reach the corpus's labels or sources

predictions.claim: The atomizer emits between 80 and 110 atoms over the target scope (the clause count).
L10 precision (atoms meeting a census clause / atoms) is at least 0.8 and measured: its threshold meets.
L10 recall (census clauses met by an atom / 82) is at least 0.9.
Each of the 12 control files yields exactly one atom, and each compiles to one intent law (4 bound, 4 access, 4 monotone).
The six controls whose truth is obstruction true get REFUTED intent laws, all reviewed faithful: control_recall is 6/6 and its threshold meets.

Of the six controls whose truth is obstruction false, the two access controls are PROVED by bool_cases and the two bound and two monotone controls are UNKNOWN; false_obstruction is empty and its threshold meets.
No PROVED control law is trivially true (TT over the control laws: 0 of 2).

On the target, between 1 and 5 atoms match a template and none compiles: no target intent law, coverage 0 of 82 (misses), compiled_coverage 0, the covering trivially-true share not_measured, and no target intent obstruction.

O10's doc-drift candidates, read by the builder in the census before this prereg, each yield an atom and no intent obstruction: Rollup.sol's '@notice Only an active submitter is allowed.' (decl_not_function: it documents a modifier), tag_advance.go's 'finalized never moves backwards' (not_solidity) and Rollup.sol's 'At most one blob is allowed: extra blobs are ignored by this hash ...' (no_template; the builder reads it as drift against `require(blobhash(1) == bytes32(0))`). O10 stays not mechanized.
The review rate is at least 0.9 (meets), and L10's overall verdict is misses (coverage misses).
SYM route (i) promotes no split of results/M3/sym (their break sets are empty).

regressions.claim: I54's outputs do not move: results/M5/l10_census_base.json, results/M5/definitions_base.json and spec/M5/preregistration.json keep their sha256 (census_sha256 and the two below).
I55 changes no file of M0-M4 (results, gen, laws other than laws/INTENT/, replay, spec/M1-M4), no frozen file and no file of I54's controls or instruments.

regressions.check: python -m unittest tests_m5.test_m5_definitions; python -m holon audit prereg --milestone M2|M3|M4|M5; python tools/freeze.py check
regressions.claim: tests_m5.test_m5_definitions keeps exactly its two I54 failures (test_p1_census_size, test_p2_census_largest_file); the M2-M5 prereg audits print PREREG OK and tools/freeze.py check prints FROZEN OK.

design.A1_comments: Solidity: a run of consecutive lines whose first non-blank characters are /// (not ////), and each /** ... */ block; Go: a run of consecutive // lines immediately followed (no blank line) by a line beginning, after indentation, with func, type, var or const. Comment markers, a leading * and indentation are removed, keeping each kept character's column in the raw line
design.A2_segments: a NatSpec tag (@ then letters, colons, hyphens) at the start of a stripped line, or a blank stripped line, starts a new segment; a segment's tag is its leading @word or null
design.A3_sentences: a segment's text (its lines joined by one space, whitespace collapsed) is cut after each '.', ';', '!' or '?' followed by whitespace or the segment's end, except a '.' that ends one of e.g, i.e, etc, vs, cf (case-insensitive) or sits between two digits
design.A4_normative: a sentence is an atom iff, lower-cased, it holds a counted marker as a whole word or phrase (bounded by non-letters). ATOM_MARKERS: must, must not, shall, shall not, should, should not, may only, can only, may not, cannot, can not, never, always, only, at most, at least, exactly, no more than, no less than, not allowed, is allowed, are allowed, forbidden, invariant, enforce, enforces, enforced, require, requires, required, ensure, ensures, guarantee, guarantees, revert, reverts, reverted. Noun-use filter: a marker among revert, reverts, reverted, require, requires, required, ensure, ensures, guarantee, guarantees, enforce, enforces, enforced does not count when the word right before it is one of the, a, an, this, that, these, those, its, their, each, any, no
design.A5_record: spec/M5/lib/intent.schema.json#/$defs/atom: id = first 16 hex of sha256('<repo>:<file>:<first line>:<sentence index>:<text>'), repo, commit (null for a control), file, lines [first, last] of the sentence's own pieces, text, tag, pieces [[line, start, end], ...] (columns into the raw UTF-8-decoded line, end exclusive) whose contents joined by one space and whitespace-collapsed give text, the sentence's index in its segment, decl (the declaration line the comment run documents: the next non-comment, non-blank line, its kind (function, modifier, contract, interface, library, event, error, struct, enum, func, type, var, const, other) and name) and the markers counted
design.A6_output: results/M5/intent/atoms.json (atoms_document): scope_commit, scope {repo: {commit, files, unresolved}}, atoms (the target scope, sorted by file, lines, id) and controls (the control atoms, each with control set to its id). `python -m holon intent atomize [--check]`
design.I1_independence: (a) the static import closure of holon.intent.atomize (tests_m5/_i55.closure) holds no holon.m5 module and no file naming l10_census or holon.m5; (b) under an audit hook, `python -m holon intent atomize` opens no path, passes no argument and writes no subprocess input that names l10_census; (c) in a git worktree of HEAD with results/M5/l10_census_base.json deleted, the atomizer writes bytes identical to results/M5/intent/atoms.json
design.I2_truth_blind: under an audit hook, `python -m holon intent compile` and `python -m holon intent run` open no spec/M5/controls/intent/*.json and no results/M5/l10_census* file; only `python -m holon intent metrics` reads them
design.L1_inputs: results/M5/intent/l10_inputs.json: census = results/M5/l10_census_base.json's clauses (read here only); atomized = the target-scope atoms projected to atom_clause (the census's scope: control atoms are not in it); laws = every record projected to intent_law (law = law_id); controls = the 12 control documents of spec/M5/controls/intent/i_*.json. tests_m5/_i55.l10_inputs assembles the same document
design.L2_output: results/M5/intent/l10.json: {l10: holon.m5.metrics.l10(inputs) (equal to tests_m5/_i54.l10), trivially_true: {covering, controls} (TT), pooled_precision (precision with the control atoms added to atomized, secondary), corpus_recall: {label: not_measured, reason: no corpus-truth key}, inputs_sha256, census_sha256, controls_sha256}. `python -m holon intent metrics [--check]`
design.M1_model: gen/M5/intent/model/<C>.bend, generated from C's transitions document: Base, the factory's 256-bit word prelude (holon.sorts.prelude3.PRELUDE, raw), St, X_<a>, chk_<a>, post_<a>, ret_<a>, and the lane's statement helpers. Supported terms: param, caller, scalar storage, env, integer literals, + - * / % (Solidity's checked semantics through their fits-256 panics), == != < <= > >=, !, &&, ||, ?, and fits 256 of + - *. Anything else (mappings, arrays, external calls, assembly, other widths) is model_unsupported for the actions that hold it
design.O_obstruction: an intent obstruction is a record with status REFUTED that passes W1 and W2 (faithful, reviewer other than compiler). An unreviewed or unfaithful REFUTED law is not an obstruction and produces no finding (the plan's risk). results/M5/intent/obstructions.json lists them, target and controls apart
design.R1_prove: gen/M5/intent/<law_id>/LAWS.bend holds exactly the law <law_id lower-cased> and imports the model; PROOF.bend comes from the first proof class that Bend accepts: computation (open s and every x_<a>, then {==}), then bool_cases (the maximal stuck Bool atoms of holds after unfolding the model, at most 12, abstracted into a lemma proved by exhaustive match, then instantiated). PROVED iff Bend prints ALL PROOFS CHECK first, exits 0 and the law is present
design.R2_refute: the witness search evaluates holds on the compiled lane model (bend -o .mjs, run by node), never on the controls' truth or any oracle: every W field of s and of each x_<a> ranges over V = {0, 1, 2, 3, 100, 2^160 - 1, 2^256 - 1} with every integer literal k of C's actions and k - 1, k + 1 (mod 2^256), in lexicographic order of the fields, at most 50000 candidates per law. The first candidate where holds is False becomes the counter-law cl_<law_id lower-cased> (exs form, BEND_PRIMER 5.4); REFUTED iff Bend accepts it
design.R3_unknown: otherwise UNKNOWN, with the bound (candidates searched) and the attempts (each proof class's failure); its proof directory is removed
design.R4_record: results/M5/intent/records/<law_id>.json (spec/M5/lib/intent.schema.json#/$defs/record): status, evidence {law, marker, law_present}, verdict (BendTT's marker when the second kernel is available, else null), proof_class, witness, bound, attempts, trivial, review, statement_hash, paths, obstruction. `python -m holon intent run [--check]`
design.S0_scope: the measured scope is L10's census.scope, recomputed by the lane itself (holon.intent.scope): the .sol and .go paths cited as <path>:<line> by spec/M2/facts/*.extracted.json and spec/M3/facts/*.extracted.json at scope_commit, read through git at each document's target.commit in the checkout config/holon.json extract.sources names; an absent path is unresolved. The controls are spec/M5/controls/intent/i_*.sol at the bytes pinned in controls_sha256 (a control's id is its file stem). The lane reads a control's .sol only: never its .json (which holds the truth), except in the metric stage (L1). A control's file stem carries its truth (_right_ / _wrong_): the lane uses an id only as an opaque label, and no module of holon/intent names either word
design.S_statement: binders: s: M.St (every scalar of C's storage, one W each: A-env makes the pre-transaction storage free) and x_<a>: M.X_<a> per action a (its parameters, the caller and the env terms it reads, one W each). holds is a Bool term (tests_m5/_i55.term_problems): bound: or(not(chk_f(s, x) == 0), le_pct(ret_f(s, x), n, x.<of>)), le_pct(r, n, a) the exact r * 100 <= n * a on 288-bit products; access: or(not(chk_f(s, x) == 0), w_eq(x.caller, s.<role>)); monotone: the conjunction over the actions a of or(not(chk_a(s, x_a) == 0), w_ge(post_a(s, x_a).<var>, s.<var>)). The law is {holds == True{} : Bool} for all binders. chk_a is 0 when every check, guard and panic of a's order holds, else 1 + the index of the first that fails; post_a and ret_a are a's post-state and return value
design.T1_templates: a sentence is matched after removing its leading NatSpec tag, lower-casing, collapsing whitespace and removing one trailing '.', ';', '!' or '?'. bound: ^(the )?<subj> (is|are) (at most|no more than) <n> percent of (the )?<of>$; access: ^only (the |an? )?<role> (can|may) <verb>( .*)?$ or ^only (the |an? )?<role> (is |are )?allowed$; monotone: ^(the )?<var> (never decreases|never moves backwards|is non-decreasing)$ (<subj>, <of>, <role>, <var>: letters and spaces; <n>: digits; <verb>: letters). At most one template matches (they are disjoint by their first words); no other sentence compiles
design.T2_binding: a matched atom compiles only when its file is a .sol file, its decl is a function of a contract C in that file, C's transitions document is extracted by the factory's frontend (holon.frontends.solidity, a generated transitions sidecar: target.commit the atom's commit, null for a control) and the lane model (M1) supports every action the law needs. Names are normalized (lower case, non-alphanumerics removed). bound: the function returns exactly one value, the first word of <subj> is the function's normalized name, <of> normalizes to one parameter's name; the law is over that function. access: <role> normalizes to one address scalar of C's storage; the law is over the documented function. monotone: <var> normalizes to one uint scalar of C's storage; the law is over every external or public non-view action of C. A failure is recorded with its reason: no_template, not_solidity, decl_not_function, extraction_failed, binding_failed, model_unsupported
design.T3_law: laws/INTENT/L_intent_<atom id>.json (spec/M5/lib/intent.schema.json#/$defs/intent_law, holon-intent/0.1): exactly one clause (the atom it was compiled from), the template, the binding {noun, name, percent}, the actions, the facts document and its sha256, the model, the statement {binders, holds} and a generated plain reading. statement_hash = 'sha256:' + sha256(canonical_json({ir_version, law_id, template, clauses, facts_sha256, statement})); laws/INTENT/REGISTRY.json maps each law to it. results/M5/intent/compile.json holds one compile_entry per atom (target and control). `python -m holon intent compile [--check]`
design.TT_trivially_true: a PROVED law is trivially true iff (a) its twin, the same statement with every action function (chk_<a>, post_<a>, ret_<a>) replaced by a universally quantified function binder of the same type, is PROVED by a proof class of R1, or (b) no inhabitant is accepted: the lane cannot show, by an exs law that Bend accepts at a witness from R2's search, a state and arguments at which every action of the law succeeds (chk_<a> == 0). trivial.twin is PROVED, UNKNOWN or not_run (a law that is not PROVED); trivial.inhabited is null when not PROVED. Reported beside coverage: the share of the laws that make coverage (pass W1-W3 and cover a census clause) that are PROVED and trivially true, and the same share over the control laws that pass W1 and W2 (tests_m5/_i55.trivially_true)
design.V_review: results/M5/intent/review_requests.json lists, per law, exactly {law_id, clause (verbatim), documents (the decl line), reading, statement (LAWS.bend's law)}; it holds no control id and no truth. Exactly one fresh reviewer, with no context beyond spec/M5/lib/intent_review_prompt.md followed by the requests, answers once; the answer is recorded verbatim in spec/M5/intent/reviews.json (reviews: reviewer 'fresh-reviewer-1', compiler 'holon.intent.compile', the prompt's and the requests' sha256, a disclosure). A law gets verdict absent when it is missing from the verdicts or when the requests' sha256 differs from the recorded one. The reviewer is disclosed as a fresh session of the builder's family
design.Y_route_i: results/M5/intent/sym_route_i.json (route_i): one entry per split of results/M3/sym/pi.json and tau.json; a split is promoted by route (i) iff its break set is non-empty, its family is pi, and an access law whose role normalizes to the split's role, whose actions meet the split's, and whose record is PROVED and passes W1-W3 marks it; tau has no intent template. tests_m5/_i55.route_i recomputes it. Nothing under results/M3/ changes
design.determinism: every output is json.dumps(obj, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + newline or generated Bend; sorted iteration, no timestamps; --check regenerates and compares bytes (run --check into a temporary directory)
design.doc: How the intent lane (holon/intent/) is built and scored. Fixed before the build; the contract tests in tests_m5/test_m5_intent.py check each rule. A rule that turns out wrong is reported under Surprises, never edited.

thresholds.measured_by: spec/M5/preregistration.json definitions.L10 (key I54); its thresholds are I54's and are not restated or moved here

I55.title: I55: the intent lane: doc comments atomized with exact spans, reviewed clauses compiled to laws/INTENT/ over the factory's extracted model, intent obstructions, SYM route (i), and L10 computed by I54's definition
